prompt.text:
Image 1 is the HEAD to draw on: the character without hair, on a transparent background, in a 1024x1024 frame. Image 2 is the GUIDE for Image 1, in the same frame and at the same scale: the light-blue area is where the hair on the skull goes; the dark-blue line is the hair's lower edge along the forehead and the temples, and the short dark-blue line running up from its highest point is the centre parting; the two dark-blue dots are where the hair meets the top of each ear; the turquoise areas on both sides are where the locks hang BEHIND the ears and behind the jaw; the red areas (brows, eyes and both ears) must stay completely free of hair. Image 3 is a STYLE sample of the same character's painted body: it shows the line weight, the cel shading and the level of detail to match. Image 3 contains no hair and is not part of the result.

Edit Image 1: add a new hairstyle on the head and change nothing else. Keep the frame, the position, the scale and the transparent background exactly as in Image 1: no shift, no zoom, no tilt, no crop. Keep the face, the eyes, the brows, the nose, the mouth, the ears, the jaw, the skin, the neck and every outline of Image 1 exactly as they are.

THE HAIRSTYLE: soft nape locks with a centre parting. A clear centre parting runs from the middle of the hairline up over the top of the head. From the parting the hair falls in two soft, smooth curtains to each side, leaving the forehead open in the middle, and frames the temples. Behind each ear the hair continues down in soft, gently curved locks that hang behind the ear and behind the jaw and end in a few soft, rounded tips at the level of the jawline. Each ear stays fully visible in front of the hair, with its own outline unchanged; the jaw's outline stays in front of the locks. No hair lies on the forehead's open middle, the brows, the eyes, the ears, the cheeks, the chin or the neck, and nothing reaches the shoulders.

SHAPE: the hair fills the light-blue area of Image 2 over the whole skull; its lower edge lies exactly ON the dark-blue line, with no band of bare skull between the line and the hair; the parting follows the short dark-blue line. The locks fill the turquoise areas and end where they end. Nothing in the red areas. Nothing below the turquoise areas.

STYLE: paint the hair in the same hand as Image 1's face and Image 3's body: the same confident dark outline of the same weight, the same cel shading in a few clear value steps, a little shadow along the parting and where the locks pass behind the ears, highlight shapes that follow the skull's rounding and the locks' fall, the same level of detail. Not photoreal, no texture noise, no soft airbrush, no spikes, no straight-cut fringe.

COLOUR: draw the hair in neutral greyscale only (white, greys and near-black), no hue at all. The hair is a luminance map that is tinted later. Everything else keeps Image 1's own colours.

The hair is one connected shape with no detached specks. Keep at least 16 pixels of empty transparent margin on all four sides of the image.

placement: the result is registered on the base by its face (scale ±4 %, shift ±40 px in the call frame), then placed as D-371: ÷2 by the premultiplied 2×2 box at (256, 0); nothing is retouched

P1.rule: registration on the face: |scale − 1| ≤ 0.04, |shift| ≤ 40 px (call frame), mean face error ≤ 14

P2.rule: scalp covered: ≥ 98 % of the design's scalp has visible hair alpha ≥ 250 (the parting's band ±3 px is not counted)

P3.rule: brows and eyes free: ≤ 10 px of grey hair on the brows' keep-clear zone in the RESULT; 0 px on brows and eyes in the layer; ≥ 6 px gap above each brow

P4.rule: ears and face: in the RESULT ≤ 10 px of grey hair on the ears (their opaque pixels and their skin margin) and ≤ 10 px over the face below the ear tops (3 px inside its outline, the eyes excepted: P3 covers them); no hair on the ears in the layer; the ears in front (an opaque ear pixel is the base's own, a soft-edge ear pixel is exactly the ear over the hair behind it); ≤ 20 px of layer hair (alpha ≥ 32) on the face below the ear tops 3 px inside its outline (it would lie hidden behind the jaw) and ≤ 20 px below the jawline (y ≥ 433)

P5.rule: one piece: the largest piece holds ≥ 98 % of the hair

P6.rule: the base is unchanged wherever the composed hair layer is empty (pixel for pixel)

P7.rule: greyscale: ≥ 90 % of the lifted hair pixels are neutral grey (saturation < 0.12)

P8.rule: its own look at app size (÷4): silhouette IoU ≤ 0.75 with the standard hair, NH-4 and the live top knot, and ≥ 0.60 with design C

P9.rule: the shape is followed overall: ≤ 3 % of the result's grey hair lies more than 8 px outside the design's zone

P10.rule: no cut: where the VISIBLE hair ends although the result's grey hair continues (not under an ear), the longest connected run ≤ 6 px, reported for the parting, the forehead, each temple and each nape

P11.rule: no local spill: the largest connected cluster of grey hair more than 8 px outside the zone ≤ 60 px

P12.rule: no local hole: the largest connected uncovered piece of the scalp ≤ 40 px (the parting's band excepted)

P13.rule: the planned nape locks: on each side ≥ 70 % of the lock zone behind the ear (y 330–412) is visible hair, and the lock ends at the jawline (its lowest visible hair at y 405–432)
